content_voiceover: This flowchart walks through the practical workup once HLH is suspected. You branch into two parallel tracks. On one side you ask about previous HLH, a positive family history, or a known genetic mutation. On the other side you evaluate for mimics: malignancies, infections, rheumatologic disease, and other primary immune deficiencies, since secondary HLH triggers need to be ruled in or out. Both tracks converge on the question of whether ferritin and or soluble C D twenty five are elevated. If no, HLH is unlikely, except in cases of isolated central nervous system disease, which can present without the typical systemic lab abnormalities. If yes, you move into the full diagnostic evaluation panel. General HLH studies include a C B C, A L T and bilirubin, fibrinogen and coagulation tests, triglycerides, ferritin and soluble C D twenty five, and where available C X C L nine, interleukin eighteen, and T cell H L A D R, plus a bone marrow or other tissue aspirate and biopsy to look for hemophagocytosis. CNS evaluation includes a brain M R I and lumbar puncture, since CNS involvement changes management. Adjunctive studies include C T of the neck, chest, abdomen, and pelvis, P E T C T to evaluate for lymphoma, viral P C Rs for E B V, C M V, adenovirus, and H S V, and consideration of tick or mosquito borne disease testing. Rapid screening tests for primary HLH include perforin, S A P, X I A P, and C D one oh seven a expression, followed by genetic testing to confirm a familial form.
keypoints: Two parallel entry points: prior HLH or genetic mutation, versus workup for malignancy, infection, rheumatologic disease
Elevated ferritin and/or soluble CD25 triggers full diagnostic evaluation; if not elevated, HLH is unlikely except isolated CNS disease
General studies: CBC, LFTs, fibrinogen, triglycerides, ferritin, sCD25, CXCL9, IL-18, marrow biopsy for hemophagocytosis
Rapid functional screening: perforin, SAP, XIAP, CD107a expression, followed by confirmatory genetic testing
keypoint_voiceover: When HLH is suspected, check ferritin and soluble C D twenty five first. If they're not elevated, HLH is unlikely unless there's isolated CNS disease. If elevated, proceed to general HLH labs, CNS imaging with brain M R I and lumbar puncture, infectious workup, and rapid functional screening tests like perforin, S A P, X I A P, and C D one oh seven a, followed by genetic testing to confirm.
